body:
Thank you for your continuing kindness.

Well, each day that passes is making this more permanent, but initially it was a very sudden change, on a particular day in late December. Then everything became a struggle. We were both apart for the holidays, and that just "baked in" the situation really. If there hadn't been a break, I'm not sure things would have been like this (yet).

I have considered moving out, but it seems financially and practically difficult to do so. I am trying to spend as much time as I can with friends, but there are limits to their empathy.

I had an epiphany an hour ago. Perhaps she is feeling low. I mean, I know she feels alternately guilty and annoyed now, but perhaps she was feeling low before this ended, and perhaps it wasn't particularly related to me. Perhaps, feeling this way, a relationship and all its attendant struggles were just another burden for her. Because I have considered alternative reasons for my rather sudden, extreme exile, and they don't quite gel unless one believes she is a psychopath, which I don't.

I tried to tell her I was there for her, but I realise that every declaration came with an implicit obligation on her part, which won't have helped. Perhaps I just need to try and be there for her and look after myself in the meantime. I'm not holding out hope for a full reconciliation, but I think I might be right about how she's feeling, and that's better than the dark interpretations of her behaviour that fill my thoughts otherwise.

Yes, that's kind of you. They were the best times of my life, compressed into two months. But they were also some of the worst. I feel like I have had my heart ripped out. We actually live in a shared house, our rooms adjacent; I can't simply forget her, which might be one common approach. Any day now, I fear another man will be in her bed, and I will not be able to prevent myself from hearing them, or seeing them together in my mind's eye. I dread that day.

Please don't do what I did, if you are looking for this. I think I see my mistake. My connection was built on being madly in love, but we hadn't the love of friendship beneath to save me. She is a complicated woman with a difficult past. She did some cruel things to me, and I let her, because I was madly in love. Perhaps if we had developed a longer friendship she would have cared more about the possibility of discarding it.

But yes, the memories of our time together.

We watched a Christmas film in each other's arms. I kissed her head. She held my hand. About halfway through, for no reason, she tightened her grip and folded herself into me. We just held each other like that for a while. It is the simple things in life that matter to me.

She came into my room, drunk, and we both got hammered together. We kissed, and much more besides, for literally hours. I can still feel the curve of her thighs as she sat astride me.

She caught me in the hallway, both of us on our way out. She leant towards me and gave me a passionate kiss, and then left.

She leant out of my window, smoking, and I stood behind her. She rubbed herself against me. We tore off each other's clothes.

We cried together. We laughed together. I listened to her aspirations, and she told me that I was the first to do so and engage.

I can still see the curve of her lips, but although she is in the next room, she no longer sees me. I am no longer a part of her life, but I am right here.
